given: a set of sprint-1 stock rows in which some inventory_codes are full location-batch-serial codes and some are nonconforming
when: the integrity probe is run as part of accepting the change
then: it surfaces the count of nonconforming rows (those whose code could not be parsed into batch and serial) for review before the change is accepted

independence.rationale: Earlier ACs assert what the migration does to the data; AC5 asserts a separate reporting artifact, the count of nonconforming rows, is produced for review. The backfill could behave correctly while no probe count is surfaced, so this fails independently.

architectural_notes: Infra. The integrity probe is an observability concern (NFR-F6-integrity-probe): a query in app/services that counts rows whose code could not be parsed into batch and serial, surfaced for review before the change is accepted. Uses the same delimiter-only parse rule as the backfill (single source of truth, no fabrication) and reads through app/repositories. Verified on the shared UP-state verify branch over a mixed conforming/nonconforming seed by asserting the reported count equals the seeded nonconforming count. Cross-cutting: reporting/observability owned by the service layer the migration calls, never the domain entity.
